fig_grand_baseline_standing.png.caption: Per-residue detection on the official CryptoBench apo test fold (192 single-chain units, MMseqs2 10% cluster-disjoint), every method on the same residue universe in one pass. Left, mean per-unit ROC-AUC; middle, mean per-unit PR-AUC; right, the pooled residue read. The two per-unit metrics do not order the methods the same way and both are shown: our best architecture (geometry + seam, equal-z, gate r=14) leads pLM-NN on ROC-AUC (0.8341 against 0.8235) and trails it on PR-AUC (0.4280 against 0.4380). Neither margin is resolved; see the paired panel. Against P2Rank 2.5.1 and PocketMiner the lead is resolved on both metrics. Methods are drawn in the artifact's order and not sorted by any metric shown, because sorting by the metric displayed is how a figure comes to argue for the metric that flatters it. 20 of our architectures have been scored on this fold, which is the multiplicity any single margin here should be read against.

fig_grand_baseline_paired.png.caption: Paired per-unit differences, geometry + seam, equal-z, gate r=14 minus each baseline, on the 192 units where both sides are defined -- every row here has the same n_paired, so no difference in this panel mixes coverage into the comparison. Whiskers are 95% bootstrap intervals over units (10000 resamples, seed 20260802). A bar whose interval crosses zero is drawn grey whatever the sign of its point estimate, so a parity cannot be read as a win. On ROC-AUC: pLM-NN (CryptoBench's own) +0.0106 [-0.0089, +0.0297] on 103/192 units; P2Rank 2.5.1 +0.0408 [+0.0192, +0.0609] on 143/192 units; PocketMiner +0.0818 [+0.0602, +0.1030] on 155/192 units. The pLM-NN row is the one that does not resolve, in both directions and on both metrics, and it is reported as parity rather than as a lead. Rows are sorted by effect size.

n_units_definition: units where every method returned a finite per-residue vector and ROC-AUC was defined; identical across all seven methods here, so every paired row has n_paired = this number
colour_rule: an interval crossing zero is drawn grey regardless of the sign of its point estimate, so that a parity cannot be read as a win
ordering_rule: panel A keeps the artifact's order; panel B sorts by effect size, which is stated in its caption
